hypothesis: Mesh Jacobi fields and angle-defect curvature approximate the smooth ones only in the right order of limits and at vertices whose stars become regular.
mathematical_model: Smooth: j'' + K j = 0, j_head(s) = sin(s) for K = 1. Mesh: curvature is concentrated at vertices (cone points); two geodesics are rotated relative to each other only when a vertex lies between them, so the finite-difference field depends on delta/h. For vertices on a sphere the angle defect tends to K times the circumcentric (Voronoi) cell area, so defect/(A/3) tends to K Voronoi/(A/3): 3K / (4 cos^2(pi/n)) at regular valence-n stars, and a value other than K wherever the star stays irregular.
numerical_result: FD Jacobi (delta=0.1): mean error 2.16e-01, 8.07e-02, 2.40e-02, 6.25e-03, 3.21e-03, 1.17e-03 (levels 2-7, order 1.53, pairwise 1.43, 1.75, 1.95, 0.96, 1.45); delta=1e-05: 30/30 pairs on levels 2-6 share face sequences and give j = L = 2.0 (deviation 5.0e-10), error 1.0907; at level 7 (about 0.37 vertices expected in each pair's wedge) 4/6 pairs straddle a vertex. Valence-5 angle-defect curvature 1.1459056 vs predicted limit 1.1458980 (order 2.00); Voronoi valence-5 error 1.6e-05. Valence-6 max error on base-edge arcs 1.93e-03, 2.43e-03, 2.56e-03, 2.59e-03, on face medians 2.70e-03, 2.14e-03, 1.99e-03, 1.96e-03, off the mirror planes 1.09e-03, 5.39e-04, 4.33e-04, 4.65e-04 (levels 4-7); torus order 1.93. Implementation sanity check (not a finding: discrete Gauss-Bonnet holds for any closed mesh whose triangle angles sum to pi): residual 4.0e-11.
observation_model: Central difference |X+(L) - X-(L)| / (2 sin delta), exact for the smooth unit sphere; vertex curvature estimates against K = 1 or the torus closed form.

title: Compare smooth and mesh Jacobi approximations.
uncertainty: Deterministic. At intermediate delta the FD error depends on how many vertices lie between the paired geodesics (a pair that straddles a vertex jumps), so intermediate values are reported without a claim; only the two limits are asserted. The expected wedge vertex count is a heuristic for evenly spread vertices.
unresolved_assumptions: The valence-6 plateau (about 2.6e-3) lives on the icosahedral mirror planes (base-edge arcs and base-face medians). The mixed Voronoi area converges on the same vertices, so their stars stay irregular (Voronoi cell different from A/3) under refinement; why is not derived (a kink of the recursive midpoint map across base edges is a plausible cause there, and no mechanism is given for the medians), and no closed form for the plateau is given. The off-mirror maximum stops decreasing near 4.5e-4 at level 7, so pointwise convergence off the planes is not established either.
The torus grid is regular; irregular torus meshes are not tested here.
